newsitem.title: USA: Showers expected for U.S. HRW wheat regions - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Showers expected for U.S. HRW wheat regions - WSC.

text.p: Widespread showers were expected to fall across Kansas, Oklahoma, northern Texas and southern Nebraska Tuesday and Wednesday, threatening to stall wheat harvest progress, Weather Services Corp said.

"If you're a wheat farmer, you're probably going to be a little sad about this forecast," said WSC meteorologist Mike Palmerino. "It is a wet one and it looks like it could be unsettled for most of the week."
Palmerino forecast rainfall amounts of 0.50 to 2.00 inches with 70 percent coverage for the HRW belt on Tuesday and Wednesday.

"Today (Monday) looks like it will be the driest for the next five days," Palmerino said. "A cold front is going to push down into Kansas tomorrow and it's going to slowly settle southward on Wednesday. The front looks like it's going to stagnate in the HRW belt on Thursday and Friday."
Palmerino said additional accumulation was possible on Thursday and Friday.
"I would not be surprised at all if you picked up another 0.25 to 1.00 inch with maybe 50 percent coverage," he said. "This is not going to be a good week at all."
Weather patterns looked more favorable for corn and soybean development in the U.S. Midwest, Palmerino said.

Thundershowers were expected to hit the Dakotas on Monday, moving into the western Corn Belt Monday afternoon and early Tuesday. Rainfall amounts of 0.25 inches were expected with 60 percent coverage.
Storms should push eastward Tuesday afternoon and early Wednesday with 0.25 to 0.75 inches and 50 to 60 percent coverage, Palmerino said.
Temperatures were expected to remain below normal for the rest of the week.

"The cooler weather we saw develop over the weekend is going to be reinforced a bit," he said. "It probably won't be as cold as it was this weekend but the eastern corn belt may stay cool through the end of the week."
